body_html:
How it works

In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides: a² + b² = c². Baudhayana stated this in the Shulba Sutras.

To find a shorter side, subtract: a² = c² − b². If a² + b² = c² for the sides of a triangle, it has a right angle (the converse).

Whole numbers that fit, like 3, 4, 5 or 5, 12, 13, are Baudhayana–Pythagoras triples.

Example

The legs are 9 cm and 12 cm. Find the hypotenuse.

81 + 144 = 225

√225

Answer: 15 cm

Example

The hypotenuse is 25 cm and one leg is 7 cm. Find the other leg.

625 − 49 = 576

√576

Answer: 24 cm

Common mistakes

  • Adding the sides: 3 + 4 = 7 instead of √(9 + 16) = 5.
  • Adding the squares when finding a shorter side (subtract instead).
  • Forgetting to take the square root at the end.
